### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via WriteObservabilityOptions (symbol, a top-level interface))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5050442bb91feff30aa8d4211daac6158331058a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `20b027eca9197bba1e0dea98c36d5180d365b794` — the merge of head `54a1cf34b6544898ecb4606b18b83f33cf5eb2cc` into base `5050442bb91feff30aa8d4211daac6158331058a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 20b027eca9197bba1e0dea98c36d5180d365b794 && git checkout 20b027eca9197bba1e0dea98c36d5180d365b794
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5050442bb91feff30aa8d4211daac6158331058a 54a1cf34b6544898ecb4606b18b83f33cf5eb2cc && git checkout -B drift-repro 5050442bb91feff30aa8d4211daac6158331058a && git merge --no-ff 54a1cf34b6544898ecb4606b18b83f33cf5eb2cc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5050442bb91feff30aa8d4211daac6158331058a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5050442bb91feff30aa8d4211daac6158331058a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `54a1cf34b6544898ecb4606b18b83f33cf5eb2cc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/readonly-strict-errors.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-stored-expression-dropped-fields.test.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts + .changeset/25000-strict-stored-expression-refusal.md

### ① Derived judgments

**Round 2.** Round 1, at head `a8e9d3611c`, failed on one blocker: on the predicate path, `settleBulkStoredExpressions`' `ValidationError` fired before `assertNoStrictDrops()`, which broke the #5126 ordering. The branch since then is one fix commit, `0e9eba5e78`, plus two clean merges of `origin/main`. Each merge's diffs against both parents equal the other side's changes, so no conflict resolution touched unrelated logic.

**The blocker is fixed on all three paths.** Every throwing stored-expression pass sits in a `try`. The `catch` runs `assertNoStrictDrops()` and then rethrows the original error:
- **Predicate update**, `engine.ts:18836-18852`: readPriorRows, both computes and settle.
- **By-id update**, `:18527-18540`.
- **Insert**, `:16819-16831`: the catch uses the strip-only `droppedFieldEvents`. `insertMany` routes through `insert`.

At the moment of the throw, the `stored_expression` replacement is not yet in the drop set. With no strict strip drops, the original error passes through unchanged. On the no-throw path, one refusal still names every strip drop plus the replacement, with `stored_expression` last. The new ordering pin is discriminating: its non-strict control is pinned to `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

**Round 1's verified list still holds:**
- every strict refusal precedes validation and any driver dispatch;
- no other caller of `computeStoredExpressions`;
- error code `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED`;
- every other message byte-identical.

**Non-blocking:**
- by-id keeps `emitDrop` and `applyStoredExpressionsToPatch` outside its `try`, while the predicate path keeps them inside. Both are pure, so the asymmetry is cosmetic;
- insert assigns computed values onto the in-memory row copies before the refusal. Nothing reaches a driver.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql` `minor`, `fix(objectql)!`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Under the amended 「甲」 rule 2 (#6015 `6303865025`), a conversion-less narrowing of an in-process option ships as a BREAKING minor in 18.x.
- `@objectstack/spec` `patch`: TSDoc only, on shipped declarations, with no schema, `.describe()` or export change.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Wire:** no REST or wire caller can set `strictReadonlyWrites`.
- **Release text:** the pending `.changeset/24690-stored-expression-dropped-fields.md` still says strict is "unchanged … deferred to 19.0". This entry says it supersedes that bullet, and the older note is left for the maintainer's release-note decision.
- **Untouched:** `.changeset/24690-*` and `content/docs/releases/`.
- **Hand-written docs:** filed as #25089.
